all.p7_detail:
The compromise is at the BOUNDARY, and it is real -- but it is smaller than it first looks, so here is the measurement-shaped version rather than the docstring-shaped one.

WHAT IS WRONG. oja_pca.py:2 boasts "pure Python, no tensors" and :10 "Pure standard library" -- residue of the retired rule. Its only consumer is a numpy module. cortex/percept_surprise.py:90 does `residual = xv.tolist()` to demote a numpy vector to a Python list PURELY so OjaNeuron can eat it, then :94-96 runs the Gram-Schmidt deflation as a Python `for i in range(self.in_dim)` comprehension, and :67 rebuilds a fresh `(k, in_dim)` array with `np.asarray([nrn.w for nrn in self._neurons])` on EVERY `_surprise()` call. A numpy caller demoting to lists and re-promoting per call is the same class of defect as polychronization's nested-dict delay buffer: a data-structure imposed by a rule that no longer exists.

WHAT THE DEPENDENCY WOULD ACTUALLY BUY -- two different answers, and conflating them would overstate the case.
  * LIVE TICK: brain.py:1343 builds `PerceptSurprise(in_dim=len(percept), k=8)` and `percept` is the 64-dim normalized latent (brain.py:1282 "[0,1]^64", built at :1300-1302). So the live cost is 8 neurons x 64 dims ~ 1k Python float ops per tick. At n=64 numpy's per-call dispatch and allocation overhead is comparable to a list comprehension. numpy buys ~nothing here, and claiming a live speedup would be dishonest.
  * THE CORE SELF-CHECK, which is where the width is: percept_surprise._load_latents (:145-158) rate-codes the N-MNIST pack to `2*34*34 = 2312` dims, then `_run_stream` does 200 observes at k=4 (:161-172) and main() does 3 more epochs over all of class 0 (:212-214). Every one of those observes pays a 2312-element `.tolist()`, 4 x 2312 Python-loop Oja updates, 4 x 2312 Python-loop deflations, and a `(4, 2312)` array rebuild. That is the real cost, it sits on the CORE gate (and now on tests/test_selfchecks.py in-process), and vectorising it is a large factor.

So: REDESIGN_NEEDED -- accept numpy (unconditional core dep, pyproject.toml:38-49), have OjaNeuron hold `self.w` as a float64 array and accept an array, and let percept_surprise stop round-tripping. Do it as a SEPARATE commit from the move ("one change per commit with the full gate green").

THE CONSTRAINT THE REDESIGN MUST RESPECT, and it is not free. The elementwise update `w + lr*y*(x - y*w)` is bit-exact under numpy (identical IEEE754 operations, same order). The two REDUCTIONS are not: `_mathutils.dot` (:60-61) and `_mathutils.unit` (:64-66) both accumulate strictly left-to-right, while `np.dot`/`np.sum` use pairwise/BLAS accumulation -- different rounding, so the naive port silently changes every surprise number percept_surprise has ever reported. Bit-exactness is recoverable (a strictly sequential accumulation such as `np.cumsum(w*x)[-1]` matches Python's left-to-right `sum()` on float64) but it MUST BE PROVEN by an A/B against the current implementation, not assumed. `models/nmnist_pack.npz` is present on this machine, so `python -m snn_data_lake.cortex.percept_surprise` is a runnable before/after oracle -- run it. Also: oja_pca.py:99's determinism assert compares two lists with `==`; with arrays that becomes an ambiguous-truth ValueError and must become `np.array_equal(...)`. Do NOT touch substrate/_mathutils.py -- `dot`/`unit`/`mean` have many other governed list-based consumers.
all.eprop_hazard:
CLEAN, and this one matters because the module IS on a live LEARNING path (percept_surprise.py:92 calls `OjaNeuron.learn` inside `observe()`, which brain.py:1344 calls on the wake tick).

Grep of the whole file for backward|BPTT|backprop|autograd|grad|torch|numpy: zero matches. But absence of `.backward()` is not evidence of locality, so the positive argument from the code: the update at oja_pca.py:31-34 is
    y = dot(self.w, x)
    self.w = [wi + self.lr * y * (xi - y * wi) for wi, xi in zip(self.w, x)]
It reads exactly three things -- `self.w` (its OWN weight), `x` (its presynaptic input), and `y` (its OWN postsynaptic output). No other unit's weights are read, there is no transposed weight matrix, and no error signal arrives from downstream. That is genuine three-quantity Hebbian locality with no weight transport -- strictly more local than e-prop, which additionally needs a broadcast learning signal. Oja's rule needs no teaching signal at all; it is unsupervised.

The deflation in percept_surprise.py:91-96 does read the OTHER neurons' outputs (`y` and `wj` of the preceding neurons in the stack), but that is lateral inhibition within one layer, not a backward pass through a downstream layer -- Sanger's rule is standardly classed as local. No e-prop cosine-vs-BPTT obligation is triggered, because there is no gradient to compare against. Nothing here needs to be kept off a learning path.

all.p7_detail: This is the nested-dict-delay-buffer shape, not the scalar-neuron shape, and the dependency argument is already conceded inside the file. (a) The ART prototype bank is a Python `set[int]` per prototype with a FULL linear rescan of every committed prototype for every replayed triple: `:167-184` builds `scored` by iterating all `protos` and computing `len(inp & p["w"])`, run for every triple on every one of `replay_passes` passes, with `max_prototypes = 256`. The operation is exactly bit-packed popcount. Redesign: pack each template into a `(n_proto, D//64)` uint64 array; one `np.bitwise_and` plus a popcount gives `|I & w|` for ALL prototypes in a single vectorized op. This is BIT-EXACT -- `inter` and `len(p["w"])` are both integers, so the choice function `inter / (self.alpha + len(p["w"]))` (:174) is float64-identical, the `(-T, idx)` tie-break at :175 is unchanged, and the vigilance test `inter / len(inp) >= rho` (:178) is unchanged. Same precedent as polychronization today. `members` stays a Python set (it holds string tuples); only `w` becomes an array. (b) `_fbits` (:130-133) constructs a FRESH `random.Random(zlib.crc32(...))` and re-derives k positions for every token, for every triple, on every replay pass -- no memo dict. That costs nothing to fix and needs no dependency; the crc32 seeding itself must stay stdlib (it is the determinism contract). (c) The purity story is already dead inside this file: it imports numpy at :207 for the DistMult half, so the ART half being hand-rolled Python sets while the confidence half is vectorized numpy is a split in one module with no remaining justification.
all.eprop_hazard: No `.backward()`, no BPTT, no "backprop", no autograd anywhere in the file or in `reasoning/kb_ranking.py`. It DOES put a supervised gradient learner on the LIVE sleep path: `_train_distmult` at :222 runs `model.train_epoch(rows, self.dm_lr, self.dm_batch)` for `dm_epochs = 250`, and that path is live via brain.py:2667 inside `_enter_sleep`. The training rule is at `reasoning/kb_ranking.py:114-124`, hand-derived SGD -- `gp = (self._sig(sp) - 1.0)[:, None]  # d/ds -log sig(sp)` then `gEh = gp * (wr * et) + gn * (wr * en)` / `gEt = gp * (eh * wr)` / `gR = gp * (eh * et) + gn * (eh * en)`. JUDGED NOT A VIOLATION, on two grounds a name grep cannot see, and the invariant's "absence of .backward() is NOT evidence of locality" is exactly why I checked rather than assumed. (1) DistMult is a SINGLE bilinear layer: there is no backward chain and no transposed forward weight matrix to transport error through. The update to each factor is a scalar error times the elementwise product of the two co-active factors -- structurally pre x post x error, a three-factor local rule, degenerate because in a bilinear model the "weight" and the "activation" are the same object. (2) The fitted embeddings are EPHEMERAL: `model` is a local in `consolidate` (:281), never persisted, never written to the lake, never a brain synapse. It only filters which candidate triples are offered to the caller. So it is a gradient-fitted CONFIDENCE GATE, not a learning path. The promoted docstring must SAY this explicitly -- today the file says only "no rate-ANN backprop" (:40), which is the inference the invariant forbids relying on.
